the alloys containing small amount of Nb (0.5Nb and 0.1Zr) show the D03 single-phase microstructure
these second phase particles were C14-type Fe2Nb for the Nb-added alloys
C14-type Fe2Zr for Zr-added alloys
After annealing, the rolled alloys exhibited a recrystallized microstructure containing coarse second phase particles
Second phase particles with a size of ~5µm are observed for the alloys containing more than 1.5 at.% Nb or 0.5 at.% Zr
grain sizes of the alloy containing coarse second phase particles (e.g., Fe-28Al-0.5Zr) are obviously small compared with that of the alloy with single phase microstructure (e.g., Fe-28Al-0.5Nb)
The fracture surface of the alloy with a single-phase microstructure (e.g., Fe-28Al-0.5Nb) shows brittle quasi-cleavage fracture patterns
that of the alloy containing the second phase particles (e.g., Fe-28Al-0.5Zr) shows intergranular fracture patterns accompanied with a minor part of quasi-cleavage fracture patterns
that of the Fe-28Al-0.5Zr alloy containing particles shows ductile dimple patterns

the observed fine-grained recrystallized microstructures are attributed not only to the pinning effect of the second phase particles but also to the particle stimulated nucleation (PSN) of recrystallization

mechanisms.name: grain boundary pinning by second phase particles

evidence.quote: these second phase particles are effective in reducing the grain sizes in recrystallized microstructures
the particle-matrix interface may act as a dislocation sources and consequently provide a number of dislocations responsible for the plastic deformation
deformation behavior in a fine-grained microstructure is homogeneous, resulting in the increased strain to fracture
It is suggested that Nb in the solid solution has also the effect of enhancing both tensile ductility and tensile strength of Fe3Al alloys
